I am 63 years old. I never went to school, not one day. Everything I know I learned from doing it with my own hands and from watching my mother-in-law and my neighbors. My old man and I have farmed here in Quzhou for 40 years. We have 16.1 mu of land, just the two of us now. We are getting old, so we hire tractors to plow and combines to harvest. I cannot carry heavy things like I used to.

My wheat is already in the ground — I sowed 14 mu last October. I used the same improved seed as last year, about 30 jin per mu. When I sowed, I spread one 50-jin bag of compound fertilizer on each mu. I always do it this way. Now it is spring and the wheat is greening up. This week I will spread half a bag of urea on every mu, that is about 20 jin per mu. I irrigate three times: I already watered before winter, now I will water at green-up, and one more time when the grain is filling. The well pump costs electricity, but if I skip it and the weather turns dry, the harvest is finished. I spray twice: once for weeds right after sowing, and once now in April for aphids. Last year I got about 900 jin per mu, and if no hail or flood comes, I should get the same.

After we cut the wheat in early June, I will plant summer corn on those same 14 mu. I buy hybrid seed from the dealer in town — one bag is enough for one mu. I do not till the land for corn; I plant straight into the wheat stubble. I put one bag of compound fertilizer per mu at sowing, and then another half bag of urea when the corn is knee-high. Corn needs water when it tassels, so I will irrigate twice. I spray two times for armyworms. Last year my corn made about 1,100 jin per mu.

I still keep 2.1 mu of cotton. I will plant it next week. I use 3 jin of seed per mu. I rotary-till first, then put one bag of compound fertilizer down. Cotton needs a lot of care — I water three times and spray about 10 times for insects and diseases. When it starts flowering, I topdress with urea and I add some extra potassium fertilizer because cotton likes that. Picking cotton is hard on my back, but I have grown it my whole life and I know what it needs. I expect about 400 jin of seed cotton per mu.

I watch what my neighbors do. If Lao Wang across the road puts more fertilizer and his wheat looks greener, I notice. Fertilizer is expensive now — a bag of compound costs more than 130 yuan — but I would rather use a bit too much than too little. A bad harvest means borrowing money or going hungry, and I am too old for that worry. So this year I will do the same as last year. Change is risky when you have lived through bad years.
